key_insight: Learning physically interpretable fractional-step operators separately improves fluid-flow predictions over a single full-step neural operator.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables fast CFD surrogate inference across varying geometries, with approximately 1,000× lower per-step inference time than the Monte Carlo solver at comparable error.
method: Split each time step into physical substeps and train separate operators using solver-generated intermediate states.
Use conditional-linear Fourier neural operators with linear state mappings conditioned nonlinearly on inputs such as boundary geometry.
Apply symmetry sampling and corrective cycling to mitigate autoregressive error accumulation.
evidence_signal: Experiments on 2D and 3D flows with varying geometries and initial conditions report 68% and 40% reductions, respectively, in mean relative L2 rollout error versus a single full-step neural operator.
watch_item: Training requires access to solver-generated intermediate states, which may complicate integration with existing CFD pipelines.
paper_title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
